fullPassage: In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to "dad jokes." After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter. The participants then rated how funny the jokes were. Jokes with no laughter didn't get high ratings. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent funnier. And jokes followed by real laughter were rated 20 percent funnier. This study shows that both real and fake laughter make a big difference in how funny we find jokes. It suggests that we pay close attention not just to a joke's content but also to the reaction it gets. This is because we get ready to smile or laugh when we hear someone else laughing. Essentially, laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people together. This highlights laughter's social and contagious nature.

det.korean: follow(따라오다) → followed(과거분사: 뒤따르는). 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사 후치수식
det.analysis: follow를 과거분사 followed로 변환. 'Jokes followed by fake laughter'=가짜 웃음이 뒤따른 농담 — 앞의 명사 Jokes를 수식하는 과거분사(수동) 필요
det.tip: 명사 뒤 수식 + 수동 의미(뒤따라진) → 과거분사 followed

questions.passage: Jokes with no laughter didn't get high ratings. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent __________ (funny).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: funny(형용사: 웃긴) → funnier(비교급: 더 웃긴). '10 percent + 비교급' 정도 비교 구조
det.analysis: funny를 비교급 funnier로 변환. 'rated 10 percent funnier'=10퍼센트 더 웃기게 평가됨 — 'percent' 뒤 정도 비교이므로 비교급 형태 필요
det.tip: 10 percent __________ → 정도 비교 → 비교급 funnier

questions.passage: In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to "dad jokes." After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter. The participants then rated how funny the jokes were. Jokes with no laughter didn't get high ratings. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent funnier. And jokes followed by real laughter were rated 20 percent funnier. This study shows that both real and fake laughter make a big difference in how funny we find jokes. It suggests that we pay __________ not just to a joke's content but also to the reaction it gets. This is because we get ready to smile or laugh when we hear someone else laughing. Essentially, laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people together. This highlights laughter's social and contagious nature.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: no attention=무관심 / little interest=적은 관심 / quick notice=빠른 알아챔 / close attention=세심한 주의
det.analysis:
① no attention: 무관심하면 뒤 'not just ~ but also'와 모순
② little interest: 적은 관심 — 강조 흐름과 반대
③ quick notice: 빠른 알아챔 — 문맥과 어색
④ close attention: 내용뿐 아니라 반응에까지 세심한 주의를 기울인다 ←정답
det.tip: pay __________ to A and also to B(A뿐 아니라 B에도) → pay close attention(세심한 주의)

questions.passage: In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to "dad jokes." After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter. The participants then rated how funny the jokes were. Jokes with no laughter didn't get high ratings. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent funnier. And jokes followed by real laughter were rated 20 percent funnier. This study shows that both real and fake laughter make a big difference in how funny we find jokes. It suggests that we pay close attention not just to a joke's content but also to the reaction it gets. This is because we get ready to smile or laugh when we hear someone else laughing. Essentially, laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also __________. This highlights laughter's social and contagious nature.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: makes them boring=지루하게 만들다 / hides their feelings=감정을 숨기다 / brings people together=사람들을 하나로 모으다 / wastes their time=시간을 낭비하다
det.analysis:
① makes them boring: 지루하게? funnier와 모순
② hides their feelings: 감정을 숨긴다? 문맥과 무관
③ brings people together: 웃음은 농담을 더 웃기게 할 뿐 아니라 사람들을 하나로 모은다 ←정답
④ wastes their time: 시간 낭비? 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 바로 뒤 'social nature(사회적 성질)'가 단서 → brings people together(사람들을 하나로)
